title: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT outputs by default—but only in the EU
gist: OpenAI will default-on watermarking of ChatGPT text in the EU for AI Act compliance (textGrain), with it off by default elsewhere. OpenAI's own tests show 92% detection but large drops when text is edited.

insights.claim: OpenAI will automatically watermark ChatGPT text output in the EU to comply with the EU AI Act, while offering the feature elsewhere but off by default; rollout is 'in the coming weeks'.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Regulation is driving default product behavior; compliance costs differ by region.

insights.claim: Anthropic introduced text watermarking in August and enabled it globally, whereas OpenAI enables it by default only where regulators require, at least in the ChatGPT and Codex apps, and keeps it optional in the API.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Diverging compliance strategies between the two labs.

insights.claim: OpenAI's proprietary textGrain watermark achieves a 92 percent detection rate in its tests, but changing 10 percent of the text cuts detection by almost 30 percent and changing 20 percent by almost 75 percent.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Easy to defeat by light editing, limiting enforcement value.

insights.claim: No completely effective and reliable AI content marking method exists; standards such as SynthID and C2PA are relatively easy to circumvent.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Compliance does not equal effective detection; expect continued regulatory and tooling churn.

insights.claim: OpenAI will give the textGrain detector only to a limited number of researchers and organizations through a request-for-approval process.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Restricted detector access limits third-party verification.
